name: Architect
title: Architect (B.Arch)
intro: From Class 12 with Physics and Maths to a registered architect: NATA or JEE Main Paper 2, a 5-year B.Arch with built-in practical training, then Council of Architecture registration.

phases.title: Class 12 with Physics and Maths
phases.summary: Physics and Mathematics are compulsory for B.Arch; practise drawing early.
points: Class 12 with Physics and Mathematics as compulsory subjects, with the aggregate marks CoA sets in its admission rules.
A 10+3 diploma with Mathematics is a separate eligible route.
Check the current CoA admission rules for the third subject and marks; start sketching and drawing practice early.

phases.title: NATA or JEE Main Paper 2
phases.summary: Aptitude, drawing and maths — many students take both.
points: NATA is conducted by the Council of Architecture and used by many colleges.
JEE Main Paper 2 (B.Arch) is used for NITs and some centrally funded institutes.
Both are accepted for B.Arch, so many students take both.

phases.title: Counselling and admission
phases.summary: State, JoSAA or institute counselling that accepts your score.
points: Admission is through the state, JoSAA or institute counselling that accepts your NATA or JEE Paper 2 score.
Confirm each college's accepted score before choosing.
Keep your Class 12 marks proof ready — CoA sets the aggregate.

phases.title: B.Arch (5 years) with practical training
phases.summary: Design studios, construction, history and services, with practical training built in.
points: The 5-year B.Arch covers design studios, construction, history of architecture and building services.
Practical training is built into the B.Arch programme.
Build a portfolio of studio work through the course.

phases.title: Register with CoA and practise
phases.summary: Registration is required to use the title "architect".
points: Under the Architects Act, 1972 only people registered with the Council of Architecture may use the title "architect".
Work in design firms, with developers, CPWD/PWD and urban bodies, or start your own studio; government architect posts come through UPSC/state PSC recruitment.
Growth path: junior → project architect → associate → principal / own practice; or specialise with M.Arch/M.Plan.
